result.title: GeoPilot: Diagnosis-Guided Interventions and Geometric Evaluation for Aerial Reconstruction
result.summary: When a mesh reconstructed from aerial remote-sensing imagery disagrees with reference geometry, deciding what to change requires a diagnosis of the reconstruction process. We present GeoPilot, a workflow that turns diagnostics and prior observations into executable program or camera-configuration interventions. A large language model proposes the change, numerical tools reconstruct the mesh, and an external evaluator measures its geometry under a stated coordinate and reference protocol. The main case tests a shared-intrinsics hypothesis proposed before the comparison. On 224 Metashape-raster development images, shared intrinsics improved all six native-coordinate measures and reduced mean surface-to-reference distance by 7.04%. Reference-assisted alignment fitted and evaluated on separate within-scene checkerboard samples reversed the mean-distance ranking, limiting that gain to native-frame delivery. A separate matched comparison on publisher-undistorted images favored fixed published cameras on all six measures, reducing mean distance by 12.11%; the cameras retain upstream image and laser-scanning adjustment information. With one reconstruction per configuration, these comparisons provide conditional evidence for camera handling. Three end-to-end runs each delivered a mesh and six-metric evaluation from all 327 images of a second development scene.

AI.brief_summary: GeoPilot 面向航空遥感影像的三维网格重建，把诊断结果转化为可执行的程序或相机配置干预，由 LLM 提出改动、数值工具重建、外部评估器按指定坐标与参考协议度量几何，并在若干开发场景上比较共享内参假设与发布相机的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「诊断—干预—外部评估」闭环与参考辅助对齐使平均距离排序反转的发现，可能可供核查 LVR 中几何保真度评价协议与干预贡献归因的稳定性；但对象是摄影测量网格而非视觉推理内部状态，联系偏间接。
